definition-dropped.answer: §2002:4 defines method as 'A procedural entity defined by a method definition within, or inherited by, a class definition'; 2023 drops the entry and describes methods at §2023:9.3.4, whose text is word for word §2002:9.3.4. The rule speaks of a method prototype (§2002:9.3.6: 'Method definitions within an interface definition define method prototypes'), unchanged, so the programs it governs (OVERRIDE on a METHOD-ID in an interface) are the same.

pending-clause.answer: §2002:9.3.5 (Method invocation) binds an invocation by method-name up the inheritance hierarchy at runtime; 2023 renumbers it 9.3.6 and adds parametric polymorphism (signature resolution, 2023 9.3.5). The rule is a compile-time prohibition of OVERRIDE in a method prototype and rests on no invocation or resolution text, so the 2002 difference does not reach it; the refusal at --std 2002 stands as evidence.
